The repro is about opaque types with lifetimes that become unsound when reused in signatures, and this file owns inference-time definition of local opaque types, hidden-type recording, and the checks that the defining body is allowed to define them.

This file validates instantiated hidden types against an opaque type's defining form and bounds, including generic arguments and regions, so it is a likely site for missing lifetime-constraining checks that would let `Ty<'_>` flow into `fn`/`dyn Fn` positions unsafely.

The trace hits `explicit_item_bounds` and `predicates_of` for the opaque item, and this file computes and elaborates the predicate bounds attached to opaque types, making it a plausible source of the missing constraint on late-bound lifetimes.

The bad inputs use `Ty<'_>` inside function signatures and trait-object syntax, so generic-argument validation and lifetime handling during AST-to-ty conversion are relevant, especially for detecting whether the anonymous lifetime should be rejected as unconstrained.

This is the main AST-to-`ty` conversion layer for paths, trait objects, and generic arguments; the repro exercises exactly those syntactic forms when building `fn(Ty<'_>) -> &str` and `dyn Fn(Ty<'_>) -> &str`.

The query trace includes `check_item_well_formed`, and the regression is fundamentally about whether the opaque alias and its uses are well-formed under lifetime rules, so this is a credible enforcement point for the missing rejection.

The trace also exercises `implied_outlives_bounds`, and the bug hinges on whether the opaque lifetime is properly constrained; this module orchestrates outlives inference and exposes the per-item inferred predicates used to validate those bounds.

This helper drives the implied-outlives query for a well-formed type, which is directly relevant to deciding whether the late-bound lifetime carried by the opaque alias is actually constrained before being used in a signature or trait object.
